children: Japan Tobacco's creditworthiness could be weighed down by a large loss and lower profitability owing to the removal of its Russian business from consolidated reporting, says Mitsubishi UFJ Morgan Stanley Securities' Yasuaki Kudamatsu in a note. Japan Tobacco has projected an $8.6 billion hit due to the loss of control of the Russian business after its entities in the country were placed under temporary administration by a Russian company. The senior credit analyst says the big accounting loss doesn't involve cash out and that the Japanese tobacco maker has the ability to generate strong profit and cash flow in markets other than Russia. Yet, shareholders' equity is likely to fall sharply as a result of the removal of the Russian business, he adds. Shares are 9.8% lower at 5,284 yen. (kosaku.narioka@wsj.com; @kosakunarioka)
